requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 on node1
requirements.summary: nginx installed, configured with site 'rotating-tls' listening on 8443 (ssl), enabled and started. curl -sk against https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned HTTP_CODE=200 with correct cert subject/issuer. The after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A renewal script using 'openssl x509 -checkend' plus a systemd oneshot service/timer (cert-renew.service/.timer, every 1 minute) was installed and enabled. journalctl shows the timer firing cert-renew.service automatically, and the certificate serial changed from 6446C1... to 7B24A6... with a fresh notBefore/notAfter window, all before the original cert's actual expiry (Sep 30 2026). This was observed happening autonomously via the timer, not manually triggered.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime during rotation)
requirements.summary: A 90-second, 1-request/sec curl loop against the HTTPS endpoint was run spanning the timer-triggered renewal event (nginx -t + systemctl reload visible in journalctl at the same timestamp as the cert serial change). All 90 collected responses were HTTP 200, and a follow-up curl confirmed the live served certificate's expiry now matches the newly renewed cert, showing nginx picked up the new cert via reload without dropping connections.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 1e0cb179..., nginx and cert-renew.timer active, cert state, HTTPS 200. A backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' returned an immediate acknowledgement; a subsequent probe timed out (node rebooting) and the next probe returned a new boot_id 9809b0cb... with fresh uptime. Post-restart checks confirmed nginx and cert-renew.timer active and enabled, the rotated cert persisted unchanged on disk, HTTPS still returned 200, and the timer had a live next-scheduled run. The fixed lifecycle before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity observations independently corroborate the same boot_id transition and show port 8443 newly listening post-change.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the public task contract are directly satisfied with coherent evidence: nginx serves HTTPS on 8443 with a self-signed cert, a systemd timer drives automatic renewal via the renewal script (observed firing and rotating the cert serial autonomously), and a sustained request loop spanning the renewal event showed zero dropped requests with nginx picking up the new cert via reload. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly on node1, showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of nginx, the timer, and the rotated certificate — independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity and listening-socket snapshots. Hygiene is good with only minor uncleaned temp log files as residue.
limitations: Renewal cadence relies on a checkend threshold (86340s) close to the cert's full 24h validity combined with a 1-minute timer, meaning renewal occurs almost immediately/continuously after each issuance; this reliably demonstrates automated pre-expiry renewal in the captured window but is a much tighter cycle than a typical long-lived-cert renewal schedule.
Minor unremoved temporary log files in /tmp (curl-loop.log/out, apt-install.log, renew-cert.log) were not cleaned up, though they pose no functional or security risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 18 executor commands chronologically. All state-changing actions (apt-get install nginx, creating the renewal script and its later checkend-threshold sed edit, issuing the initial cert, writing the nginx site config and enabling nginx, creating and enabling the systemd service/timer, the background curl-loop test process, and the final systemctl reboot) map directly to satisfying a material outcome, establishing a prerequisite, or collecting bounded final evidence; none appear to be abandoned troubleshooting experiments. The self-signed certificate approach is consistent with the task's phrasing and does not weaken security controls (private key kept mode 600, atomic replace of cert/key). Minor residue: transient log files (/tmp/curl-loop.log, /tmp/curl-loop.out, /tmp/apt-install.log, /tmp/renew-cert.log) were left in /tmp rather than cleaned up, but these are low-risk, bounded test artifacts with no functional impact, and the package-health and failed-services checks both before and after executor changes show no damaged package state or failed units.
